label: 300 illustrative, authored synthetic voice examples across six channel types, five themes, ten geographies and cross-functional layers. Not Takeda employee data; outcomes are not model accuracy.

voices.text: Why does every plant decide alone how to prevent an unplanned stop? At Hikari the filling line went down twice last month.
At Singen our pump failure was only found after the line downtime started. Has any Takeda site tried predictive maintenance?
Batch release at Vienna still waits on paper release records from three teams. Has another plant shortened this?
Our maintenance log at Lessines is a spreadsheet nobody reads until an unplanned stop. Who has done this better?
New operators at Los Angeles need months of cleanroom training before they can work alone. Is there a faster qualified method?
Gowning and aseptic steps are taught at Osaka from the SOP only. Has a Takeda site used VR operator training?
Last launch, batch release at Brooklyn Park took weeks because release records were collected by email.
We rebuilt the cleanroom training plan at Social Circle from scratch, then heard another plant already had one.
In the shift huddle at Linz we discuss the same equipment stopped alarms every week. Is anyone predicting them?
Operator training for new operators at Bengaluru differs from the next plant, even for the same filling process.

New role in R&D, EU: I spent weeks finding who knew the history of a process before I could act.

Mentoring helps in HR (Germany), but it does not tell the next owner why we decided a past trade-off.
